sentences.text: 2. The claimants, are the wife and children of the deceased Ramesh.

The deceased Ramesh was a pedestrian on the Hosur Krishnagiri National Highways Road, Koneripalli, Near Sakthivel house, at the time car bearing Reg. No.TN 02 BC 2317 came from Hosur in a rash and negligent manner and hit against the deceased Ramesh, due to which, the said Ramesh sustained grievous injuries and died in the hospital.
It is under these circumstances, the claim petition came to be filed before the Tribunal seeking for payment of compensation for the death of the said Ramesh.

3. The Tribunal, on considering the facts and circumstances of the case and on appreciation of oral and documentary evidence, came to a conclusion that the accident had taken place only due to the rash and https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis negligent driving on the part of the driver of the Car.

Having rendered such a finding, the Tribunal proceeded to determine the total compensation payable at Rs.17,28,000/- under various heads in the following manner:
Sl. Compensation awarded under the Amount No. head (in Rs.)
1. Loss of dependency 17,55,000 2. Loss of consortium 1,32,000 3.
Loss of Estate 16,500 4.
Funeral Expenses 16,500 5.
Less 10% contributory negligence 1,92,000 committed by the deceased Total 17,28,000
The Tribunal has fixed 10% contributory negligence on behalf of the deceased and fixed the liability as against the Insurance company.

The Tribunal directed the above compensation to be paid with interest at the rate of 7.5% p.a.
4.
The Insurance company aggrieved by the award passed by the Tribunal, has filed the present appeal questioning their liability.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 5.
The learned counsel for the appellant submitted that the deceased was not crossing the road in the zebra crossing.
He recklessly crossed the National Highway through the centre median and thus contributed to the accident, eliciting contributory negligence.
Without considering the said fact, the Tribunal has fixed the liability as against the insurance company, which is unsustainable.

Further,
the compensation amount passed by the Tribunal is highly excessive.
Hence, this court may interfere with the impugned order by setting aside the same and allow this petition.

sentences.text: The learned counsel for the claimants submitted that after considering the witnesses and documentary evidences, the Tribunal has passed award which does not warrant any interference.

7. Heard the learned counsel for the appellant and the learned counsel for respondents 1 to 3.
8.
This Court carefully considered the submissions made on either side and the materials available on record.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 9
. This Court also carefully went through the award passed by the Tribunal.
10. The short issue that arises for consideration in the present appeal is as to whether the insurance company can be saddled with the liability.
There is no dispute with regard to the fact that the deceased was crossed the road in the centre median.
Unfortunately, the driver of the car lost his control and hit against the deceased, for which, the deceased sustained grievous injuries and died.

In the light of these admitted facts, the main contention that was raised before the Tribunal is that the the deceased appears to have died due to effects of head injury and also FIR has been registered against the driver of the car.
Further, the appellant has not chosen to adduce any rebuttal evidence to disprove the case of the claimants.
Hence, this Court is not inclined to interfere with in respect of the liability.
The compensation that has been granted under the other heads are reasonable and it does not require the interference of this Court.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis M.DHANDAPANI.,J rli 11.
In the result, this Civil Miscellaneous appeal is dismissed.
The award passed by the Tribunal is hereby confirmed.
No costs.
Consequently, connected miscellaneous petition is closed.
